answer: ZK attestation at the knoll: each miner submits a groth16 proof that its post-epoch work derived from a unique seed. A falcon signature binds the proof to one hardware enclave, so cloning IDs needs distinct silicon. The harbor rejects replays, forcing attackers to rent 500 CPU-hours (~$12) per fake identity, and stake slashing doubles that. Cost scales linearly while reward stays fixed, so farming goes net-negative fast — that asymmetry is why it holds.
